story.title: Our Story — MŌRI Matcha Bar & Culture
story.description: Mori means forest. The story and philosophy behind MŌRI: an urban matcha bar that turns matcha into a small daily ritual.
story.lede: Mori (森) means forest in Japanese. A short, green, easy-to-remember name for a place that wants to make matcha part of everyday life.
story.bannerAlt: MŌRI's travertine bar with daylight coming through the windows
story.nameH: Four letters and a whole forest.
name: We wanted a name that works just as well on a cup, a shopfront and a T-shirt. Mori, Japanese for forest, speaks of matcha's plant origin and the green that fills everything.
The macron over the O is our small detail: it gives the written name character, even though it's pronounced as usual. MO-ri.
We didn't want a solemn tea house or a romantic café. We wanted an urban, fresh place with personality, one that could live in Madrid, Barcelona or any European city.
story.ideaH: Matcha as a break, not a ceremony.
story.idea: The Japanese tea ceremony is beautiful, but it isn't what happens on a Tuesday at nine. MŌRI takes the best of matcha culture and brings it into your routine: a great product, carefully prepared and served without rush, even if you only have ten minutes.

story.cupsP: Every drink in the collection has its own cup colour. The logo always stays the same; the colour changes with you.

culture.title: Matcha Culture — What matcha is and how it's made · MŌRI
culture.description: Everything about matcha: where it comes from, how it's prepared step by step, ceremonial vs culinary grade and a short glossary.
culture.lede: You don't need to be an expert to enjoy it, but knowing a little makes it even better. Here are the essentials, no solemnity required.
culture.whatH: Green tea, but the whole leaf.
what: Matcha is Japanese green tea ground into a powder. The plants are shaded for a few weeks before harvest, so they produce more chlorophyll and more L-theanine: that's where the deep green and the sweet, umami taste come from.
The leaves are then dried, stripped of stems and veins and slowly ground in stone mills. Unlike regular tea, you don't steep it and throw the leaf away: you drink the whole leaf.

gloss.text: A bamboo whisk with dozens of fine prongs. It turns powder and water into a silky foam.

Thin matcha: less powder, more water, with foam. The most common way to drink it every day.
Thick matcha, almost like paint. Lots of powder and little water, stirred rather than whisked.
